title: Huperzine A in WWOX-LoF
summary: A test of acetylcholine availability and physiological inhibitory recruitment.

graph.evidence: Spontaneous hippocampal EEG counts fell during exposure in acquired epilepsy.
graph.inference: The fixed phase order leaves shared time and vigilance effects open.
graph.hypothesis: Residual septal input and receptor reserve determine the response.
graph.experiment: Match local enzyme engagement and measure acetylcholine, inhibition and recurrence.

evidence: Across ten mice, observed events fell from 119.0 to 53.5 per recorded eight hours and reached 98.8 after withdrawal. The count fell during exposure in every mouse. A separate kindling experiment supports local cholinergic dependence.
inference: Lower CHRM1 RNA survived single-library omissions in three untreated WWOX models. Hippocampal acetylcholinesterase RNA was directionally sensitive to omissions. These data do not measure cholinergic input or native inhibition.
hypothesis: Slower acetylcholine clearance could restrain recurrence only when a sufficient local input survives and its receptors recruit effective inhibition.
experiment: Compare a second reversible inhibitor at matched local acetylcholinesterase engagement. Read acetylcholine decay, inhibitory charge and spontaneous recurrence while holding temperature, vigilance and first recruitment comparable.
limits: Retain as a research probe. The published spontaneous EEG comparison has no parallel control. The investigational formulation has adult trials. Pediatric WWOX exposure, tolerability and benefit remain unresolved.
